sources.modelKind: "rotor" — a rotorcraft generates lift regardless of forward speed and has no stall floor, which the shared fixed-wing lift/AoA/stall shape (forces.ts) cannot represent as data. sim/rotorForces.ts is the second, simple force model this class uses instead; sim/aircraft.ts's computeForcesFor is the one place that picks it. Issue #30.
sources.massKg: R44 Raven II max gross weight, 2400 lb = 1089 kg. Published spec.
sources.wingAreaM2: REPURPOSED FIELD — main rotor disc area, not a wing: pi*(10.06/2)^2 = 79.5 m^2 (33 ft rotor diameter, published spec). This class has no wing; the field exists only to satisfy the shared ClassParams schema. Read by ONE thing outside sim/rotorForces.ts: sim/forces.ts::stallSpeedIasMs (via clMaxFor), which the cosmetic ASI arc (dashboard/gaugeMath.ts::asiArcs) and the LANDED/CRASHED speed gate (game/classify.ts) both call generically for every class. rotorForces.ts itself never reads this field.
sources.wingSpanM: REPURPOSED FIELD — main rotor diameter, 10.06 m (33 ft, published spec). Not read by rotorForces.ts; present only to satisfy the schema.
sources.aspectRatio: Inert placeholder (must be positive) — no wing, no aspect ratio. Not read by rotorForces.ts.
sources.aero: The ENTIRE aero block is UNUSED BY THE ROTOR FORCE MODEL — sim/rotorForces.ts never reads params.aero. It exists only because ClassParams is one shared schema across 5 fixed-wing classes and this rotor class. cl0/clAlphaPerRad/stallAlphaRad are the one exception with a real (if indirect) effect: clMaxFor(cl0=13.7, clAlphaPerRad=0.01, stallAlphaRad=1.0) -> clMax ~= 13.71, chosen so stallSpeedIasMs(this class) computes to ~4 m/s (~7.7 kt) — not a real airfoil number, but deliberately small enough that (a) the ASI's white/green arcs (gaugeMath.ts::asiArcs, which assumes every class has a stall speed) collapse to a negligible sliver near the bottom of the dial instead of a nonsensical one, and (b) game/classify.ts's LANDED/CRASHED gate (must touch down under 1.3x this 'stall speed') reads as 'under ~10 kt groundspeed' — a reasonable controlled-hover-landing threshold for a helicopter, not an arbitrary one. postStallDecayRad/cd0/gearDragCd0/speedbrakeCd0/oswaldE/cyBeta have no live reader at all for this class (liftCoefficient/dragCoefficient/computeForces are never called on a rotor class) and are set to small, harmless placeholders purely to pass validateClassParams's positivity checks.
sources.control: The ENTIRE control block is UNUSED BY THE ROTOR FORCE MODEL — sim/rotorForces.ts reads params.rotor, not params.control (a rotor's cyclic/pedal authority does not scale with dynamic pressure the way a control surface's does, so controlAuthority()/qBar-gating do not apply). Present only to satisfy the shared schema; values are harmless placeholders (rollRateMaxRadS etc. loosely mirror params.rotor's real numbers below so a stray future reader is not misled by wildly different figures, but nothing reads them).
sources.propulsion: UNUSED BY THE ROTOR FORCE MODEL — sim/rotorForces.ts does its own altitude-density thrust scaling directly (see params.rotor below), not via forces.ts's POWER_LAPSE_MODELS. maxPowerW 183,000 W is the real Lycoming O-540 rating (245 hp) for reference only. lapseModel "none" is the honest value for 'this table is not consulted' rather than picking piston/turboprop and implying a lapse model that is not actually applied.
sources.limits.vneIasMs: 130 KIAS = 66.85 m/s — real published R44 Vne. LIVE: takeover/spawn.ts clamps a rotor spawn's speed to 0.9x this.
sources.limits.vnoIasMs: Approximate caution-band boundary for the cosmetic ASI yellow arc; no published Vno for this class (helicopters do not carry the fixed-wing Vno/Vne split the same way) — a TUNING KNOB, not a source figure.
sources.limits.vfeIasMs: Set equal to vneIasMs: this class has no flaps (see flaps below), so the white/flap-speed arc never binds.
sources.limits.gLimitPos: ~3.5 g, R44 POH-adjacent figure for reference. NOT enforced — sim/rotorForces.ts always reports gLimited: false (no structural-limit model for this class, honestly declared rather than silently clamped).
sources.limits.gLimitNeg: Real R44s prohibit negative-g / low-g pushovers (mast-bumping risk on a semi-rigid rotor) — a small negative placeholder for the same unenforced, informational-only field as gLimitPos.
sources.limits.serviceCeilingM: 14,000 ft = 4267 m published density-altitude-limited service ceiling. LIVE: takeover/spawn.ts clamps a rotor spawn's altitude to this.
sources.limits.mmo: Inert placeholder set high (0.9) so it never binds — Mach compressibility is not a concern at rotorcraft speeds. Not read by rotorForces.ts.
sources.limits.vleIasMs: Unused: gear is "fixed" (skids), so hud/format.ts::gearOverspeedFor is always false for this class regardless of this value. Set equal to vneIasMs for consistency.
sources.flaps: Single inert detent — this class has no flaps. flapDetent stays 0 for the whole flight; buildFlapDetentFields (game/flightLoop.ts) reads flaps[0].label only for the HUD's flap readout.
sources.gear: "fixed" — skids, not retractable. Always reported as fully extended (sim/forces.ts::advanceGearPosition pins gearPosition to 1 for any fixed-gear class); KeyG is inert, matching every other fixed-gear class.
sources.display: ASI 0-150 kt spans hover through just past Vne. attitudeStyle "line" (steam-gauge horizon, closest of the two available faces to a real R44 panel).
sources.rotor: TUNING KNOBS (owner live-pass candidate — the least-certain numbers in this file, per the task brief). maxThrustN 17,800 N sizes hover collective (weight / (maxThrustN * densityRatio)) to ~0.6 at sea level, the 'mid/hover collective ~= weight, more climbs, less descends' shape the brief asked for, leaving headroom to climb and altitude margin before hover becomes impossible. rollRateMaxRadS/pitchRateMaxRadS/yawRateMaxRadS (46/34/29 deg/s) and their matching *DampingPerS (3.0, a ~0.33 s time constant to reach a commanded rate) are plausible-feeling low-speed-rotorcraft numbers, not measured. dragPerVelocity 427 N per m/s (= massKg*G0/25) sizes a ~25 m/s (~4900 fpm) terminal descent rate at ZERO collective — deliberately fast to keep 'cut all power' a real emergency, while a much smaller PARTIAL collective deficit gives a slow, controllable descent (e.g. half of hover collective yields a ~4 m/s / ~800 fpm steady descent) — see sim/rotorForces.test.ts's 'controllable descent rate' assertion.
